t: You're on Old Jewry, a short one-way street in the City of London, running between Poultry and Gresham Street, in Coleman Street ward. It sits in the historic and financial heart of the capital. The caricaturist Thomas Rowlandson was born here. He became one of the best-known artists of Georgian London, famous for political satire and social observation, and he poked fun at powerful figures including William Pitt the Younger and Napoleon. Others lived on the street too: William Atkins, a Restoration-era quack who claimed a cure for gout, and later the banker and Member of Parliament John Whitmore.
